questions.question: A workflow always validates a document, extracts one fixed schema, and verifies the fields. What is the strongest starting architecture?
options: A deterministic typed pipeline
An open-ended tool-using agent
A multi-agent supervisor
A durable graph with an approval interrupt
questions.explanation: The path and operations are known before execution. A deterministic pipeline is easier to test and operate without adding model-controlled routing.

questions.question: What separates an AI agent from a single model response?
options: An agent always uses a larger model
An agent runs a bounded loop that chooses actions, observes results, and stops against an explicit goal
An agent stores every conversation forever
An agent can execute any tool without approval
questions.explanation: The defining systems behavior is the controlled feedback loop: decide, act through bounded tools, observe authoritative results, and stop under a task contract.

questions.question: What does successful MCP capability negotiation establish?
options: The client and server support specific protocol features for this session.
The server is trusted to execute every advertised tool.
The user has approved every future side effect.
Every tool annotation is accurate.
questions.explanation: Capabilities establish protocol support. Trust, authorization, exposure, and user approval remain separate host and server decisions.

questions.question: What is the core invariant of a production agentic AI system?
options: The model may propose steps, but deterministic runtime controls decide what can execute, persist, retry, and stop.
Every task must be delegated to more than one model.
A tool call is trustworthy when the model explains why it selected the tool.
The run is complete whenever the model says it succeeded.
questions.explanation: The model proposes under uncertainty. Runtime authorization, state, budget, validation, and stop controls enforce the real boundary.

questions.question: Which statement is the core safety invariant for a computer-use agent?
options: A screenshot authorizes any action visible on the page.
An observation supports a proposal; trusted code authorizes the action and verifies the result.
A model-generated plan proves that its final action succeeded.
The browser's sandbox removes the need for action policy.
questions.explanation: Pixels and semantic state are evidence. Permission and proof of success come from trusted policy, direct user intent, and fresh or authoritative observations.

questions.question: What is the core invariant of a production personalization system?
options: Every user must receive a separately fine-tuned model.
Every interaction should be retained so the profile is complete.
Each personalized effect comes from authorized, inspectable, correctable, and deletable evidence.
Personalized responses must always differ from the generic response.
questions.explanation: The system needs a defensible link from an authorized profile claim to the current effect, plus correction and lifecycle controls.
